meta.title: High-level Wave design

system.name: Wave
system.one_liner: a framework for offloading userspace system-software resource-management decisions to SmartNIC ARM cores

meta.caption_draft: High-level Wave design. Wave agents run in userspace on the SmartNIC and reach the host kernel through a shared-memory queue backed by PCIe MMIO or DMA: the Wave mechanism pushes the state the agents need over the queue and receives resource-allocation decisions back through a transaction-based API, which it then enforces on the host workload.
open_questions: greyscale is faithful to the original, but the corpus record flags 'nearly monochrome palette gives no colour cue to distinguish component types' -- switch to grey-scaffold and tint only the two Wave boxes?
Do the four crossing arrows (API Calls / Txns / Interrupts / Messages) all belong to the same queue, or should they be grouped under one labelled channel?
Which side of the PCIe band should carry the MMIO-vs-DMA choice?
meta._notes: Captured: the three stacked bands with the interconnect as a full-width row rather than an arrow, the depth-3 nesting (band > inner OS frame > box), the two Wave boxes as the only novel components, and the four named crossing channels. Not captured: the rotated arrow labels in the left gutter are recorded as ordinary edge labels plus a route_hint; the drawer decides the rotation. The 'Kernel Space' / 'Userspace' strips are annotations, not containers, because they label the two boxes rather than enclosing anything else.
